 Utah Continues Homestand, Hosts San Jose
 The Utah Mammoth will continue a five-game homestand with a Saturday night game against the San Jose Sharks
 By 
 Catherine Bogart 
 @CatherineBogart 
 November 14, 2026 
 Link copied 
 THE DETAILS
 WHO : San Jose (8-11-2) vs Utah (10-8-2)
 WHEN : Nov. 14, 2026 – 7:00 p.m. MT
 WHERE : Delta Center
 TV : Utah16, Mammoth+
 RADIO : Mammoth App, NHL App, KSL Sports Zone (97.5FM), KSL Sports App
 PRE-GAME VIDEO
 PLAYER INTERVIEW: Keller 
 COACH INTERVIEW:  Tourigny 
 TUSK TALK: Bringing Urgency 
 Bringing urgency offensively and defensively will help in Utah's game against San Jose
 MORNING SKATE NOTES
 Utah continues its homestand with a game against the San Jose Sharks
 Head coach André Tourigny gave multiple injury updates following morning skate
 Injury Updates 
 Following morning skate, Tourigny gave updates on several players:
 John Marino (upper-body, IR): “Getting better, should start practicing contact soon, very soon. Hopefully (for) our next practice.”
 Logan Cooley (upper-body): “Nothing long term, not playing today but hopefully we can have him pretty soon, day-to-day.”
 Nick Schmaltz (lower-body): “No timeline yet. We should have news soon.”
 Connected Defensively 
 Utah brought a connected defensive effort against the St. Louis Blues on Thursday. The team played with a high level of urgency and execution and this is something Utah is focused on building off of.
 “But for us, it’s the same game plan,” Tourigny explained. “I think we played with a lot of urgency, a lot of purpose defensively. We were fast, we were physical, we were in your face. Even when we gave up time, possession, we did not give them (the) opportunity to execute with time and space. They had to execute under pressure all the time and under duress and we need to maintain that…we need to buy in (with) that and be really hard defensively.”
 “I thought it was good,” Keller said of last game’s defensive effort. “We have to play like that every single night. I think the best teams in the league, that’s how they defend. They make you work for everything and that’s where we want to be and where we believe we can be. So just buying in and doing it every single night, it’s a hard thing to do, but we believe we can do it.”
 Generating Offense 
 Utah is suffering from multiple injuries to their team, including the top two goal scorers, Logan Cooley and Nick Schmaltz. However, the team has plenty of depth and can bring a greasy game to score more goals.
 “Offensively, we had a bunch of chances, so that will come,” Tourigny said. “…the chances are there, we need to hit the net, and we need to be a little bit more greasy net front, pucks at the net, rebounds, that kind of stuff. That will open up.”
 GAMEDAY
MacKenzie Weegar has recorded the second-most hits among defensemen (63) and ranks tied for the league lead with 55 blocked shots. He is the only NHL player with at least 60 hits and 50 blocked shots this season. pic.twitter.com/15yHjrSLXl 
— Utah Mammoth PR (@UtahMammoth_PR) November 14, 2026 
 GAME PREVIEW
 Tonight's Matchup 
 Utah 
 Utah is 10-8-2 this season and is 3-5-2 over the last 10 games. The team has 22 points and is in the second wild card spot in the Western Conference.
 In their last game, Utah fell to St. Louis in an eight round shootout, 1-0. Karel Vejmelka earned a shutout after he stopped all 22 shots he faced in regulation and overtime. It was a resilient effort and strong defensive performance by Utah , despite missing five starters from the lineup.
 Logan Cooley’s 11 goals lead the team, as do captain Clayton Keller’s 20 assists and 25 points. 
 Vejmelka and Sebastian Cossa make up Utah’s goaltending tandem. Vejmelka has a 6-6-1 record with a 3.02 goals-against average, a .879 save percentage, and two shutouts. Cossa has a 4-2-1 record with a 3.56 goals-against average and a .863 save percentage.
 Saturday is the second of five-straight at home for the team. Utah will host the Vancouver Canucks on Monday.
 San Jose 
 San Jose is 8-11-2 this season and is 2-7-1 over the last 10 games. The Sharks have 18 points and are fifth in the Pacific Division.
 In their last game, the Sharks lost to the Pittsburgh Penguins in a shootout, 3-2. Macklin Celebrini and Mason Marchment each had a goal in the loss. Yaroslav Askarov stopped 34 of the 36 shots he faced. 
 Celebrini’s eight goals, 15 assists, and 23 points lead the Sharks. Will Smith’s seven goals and 14 points are second on the team, while Dmitry Orlov’s eight assists trail only Celebrini. 
 Askarov and Alex Nedeljkovic make up San Jose’s goaltending tandem. Askarov has a 5-8-1 record with a 3.12 goals-against average and a .894 save percentage. Nedeljkovic has a 3-3-1 record with a 3.23 goals-against average and a .895 save percentage.
 The Sharks host the Nashville Predators tomorrow night in the second half of a back-to-back. Sunday’s game is the first of a four-game homestand for San Jose.
 By the Numbers 
 The captain of each team leads their roster with seven points over the last five games (Keller: 1G, 6A; Celebrini: 3G, 4A). Both Keller and Celebrini lead their team in points this season (Keller: 25, Celebrini: 23).
 Keller’s 25 points are 14th in the NHL, while Celebrini’s 23 are tied for 22nd in the league.
 San Jose will play its 12th road game of the year in Salt Lake City. The team’s 11 games away from SAP Center are tied for fifth-most in the NHL.
 Utah is tied with the Edmonton Oilers for most goals by defensemen in the NHL (16).
